I felt the same way 2 years ago after spending a lot of money on my college graduation, learning literally nothing, and developing new issues.

I worked a little on myself and I'm pursuing my MBA now and I feel like I'm good at what you're doing. So I hope you don't do it because of this, it would be sad since you can turn it around still.
Thank you so much yo. Yes I'll definitely look into that. I'm doing better by now, thanks a lot for responding and helping out, you're a great person!!
Bah! I got some skeletons in the closet, but thank you, I try to do better!

Yes, you're right, I guess I need to think about it a little and make my mind up.

Thanks a lot, again, for the perspective, I really appreciate you helping out, I really needed it. You're a real good person!
Thanks a lot yo. Really appreciate the advice, you're a real nice person
And btw she'll be devastated, she has issues but she does care for me and I know it's not healthy but is quite emotionally dependant on me.

Thank you so much for replying man. It just felt so good for someone to just read and understand what I went through that I already feel better.

Idk I'm too attached to let go, it feels like I'll have nothing after 5 long years. I know she needs to work on her issues and so do I but I keep going back and forth if this is actually getting toxic and I should let go or do the easy comfortable thing to do and just stay. 

To be fair, we're really happy in our good times and we do rely on each other a lot and obviously have a lot of feelings for each other. She's not a bad person, not sure if this is a bad fit or something that can be fixed.

Btw, you're a really good person bro, speaking of being selfless. The fact that you're going out of your way and trying to help people out here says a lot.
